questions.question: Define the principle of clarity and distinctness as applied to mathematical reasoning. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes holds that an idea is clear when it is present and evident to the attentive mind, and
  • distinct when it is precise and clearly separated from other ideas. Clear and distinct ideas serve as
  • the criterion of truth.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the relationship between thinking and the existence of the mind in Descartes. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes argues that thinking proves the existence of the mind. His statement “I think,
  • therefore I am” establishes that the mind exists wh enever it thinks.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Identify the essential characteristics of Spinozistic substance. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Spinozistic substance is self-caused, exists independently, and is infinite and eternal. It
  • possesses infinite attributes, of which thought and extension are known to human beings.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the meaning of apperception in Leibniz’s philosophy. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Apperception is the conscious awareness of one’s pe rceptions. It distinguishes conscious
  • mental states from unconscious or obscure perceptions.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State why the Cogito is regarded as an indubitable truth. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• The cogito is regarded as indubitable because even doubting requires thinking. Therefore, the
  • existence of the thinker cannot be denied while thinking is taking place.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Identify the basis of Descartes’ argument from the cause of the idea of God. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes argues that the idea of an infinite and perfect being exists in his mind. Since he is
  • finite and imperfect, he cannot be the ultimate cause of this idea; therefore, God must exist as its
  • cause.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define mind–body dualism according to René Descartes. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Mind-body dualism holds that the mind an d body are two distinct substances. The mind is a
  • thinking, non-extended substance, whereas the body is an extended, non -thinking substance.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define Spinoza’s philosophical conception of substance. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Spinoza defines substance as that which exists in itself and is conceived through itself. He
  • maintains that there is only one substance, God or Nature, of which everything else is a mode.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the basic claim of the Identity of Indiscernibles / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Leibniz’s principle of the identity of indiscernibles states that no two distinct things can
  • possess exactly the same properties. If two things share all their properties, they mu st be
  • identical.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define the doctrine of pre-established harmony according to Leibniz. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• The doctrine states that mind and body do not directly interact with each other. Instead, God
  • has established a harmony between them so that their states correspond perfectly.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: State the characteristics of a clear idea in Descartes’ criterion of truth. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• A clear idea is one that is present and evident to the at tentive mind. A distinct idea is precise
  • and sharply separated from other ideas, free from confusion.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Define mind–body interactionism in Descartes’ philosophy. / [CO2] [2x8 = 16]
questions.solution_html:
• Mind-body interactionism is the view that the mind and body, though distinct substances,
  • interact with each other. Descartes associated this interacti on with the pineal gland, which he
  • considered the principal seat of their interaction.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the distinction between immediate and mediate modes within the framework of Natura Naturata. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Immediate modes arise directly from the absolute nature of God’ s attributes, while mediate
  • modes arise through the influence of other modes. In Spinoza’s philosophy, motion and rest are
  • examples of immediate modes of extension, whereas the particular arrangements of physical
  • things are mediate modes. Both belong to Na tura Naturata, the totality of things that follow from
  • God or Nature.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the different grades of perception found among monads / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Leibniz distinguishes between obscure perceptions, clear perceptions, and conscious
  • awareness or apperception. Simple monads possess obscure perceptions, while animal souls have
  • memory and more distinct perceptions. Rational souls, or spirits, possess reason and
  • apperception, enabling self-consciousness and reflection.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Compare thought and extension as the principal attributes of created substances. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes identifies thought and extension as the two principal attributes of created
  • substances. Thought is the essential attribute of mind, while extension in length, breadth, and
  • depth is the essential attribute of body. They are distinct and independent in their essential
  • nature, although Descartes maintains that the mind and body interact in human beings.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain Descartes’ view that innate ideas are discovered through the mind rather than produced by sensory experience. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes holds that innate ideas are present in the mind by its very nature and are not
  • derived from sensory experience. The mind discovers these ideas through intellectual reflection
  • and reasoning. Examples include the ideas of God, mathematical truths, an d certain fundamental
  • principles.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how Deus sive Natura expresses Spinoza’s monistic conception of reality. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• The expression Deus sive Natura means “God or Nature” and expresses Spinoza’s belief that
  • God and Nature are one and the same reality. He rejects the idea of a transcendent creator
  • separate from the universe and mainta ins that everything exists within the one infinite substance.
  • Individual things are modes of this single substance, which exists through itself.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of demonstrations in establishing propositions in Spinoza’s method / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Spinoza adopts a geometrical method in which philosophical arguments are presented
  • through definitions, axioms, propositions, and demonstrations. Demonstrations establish the truth
  • of propositions by deriving them logically from previously accepted principles. This method
  • aims to provide philosophy with the systematic certainty associated with mathematics.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the transition in Leibniz’s thought from scholastic influences to a modern philosophical framework. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Leibniz was influenced by scholastic philosophy, particularly its concepts of substance, form,
  • and metaphysical explanation. He combined these traditional ideas with modern developments in
  • mathematics, physics, and rationalist philosophy. His theory of mona ds and principle of
  • sufficient reason reflect his attempt to construct a systematic modern metaphysics.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the correspondence between the order of ideas and the order of bodily events in Spinoza. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Spinoza maintains that the order and connection of ideas are the same as the order and
  • connection of things. The mental and physical worlds are two e xpressions of the same
  • underlying reality, viewed through the attributes of thought and extension. Therefore, mental
  • events and bodily events correspond without directly causing one another.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the intellectual background of the rise of Rationalism in Modern Philosophy. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Modern rationalism emerged during the seventeenth century in r esponse to the search for
  • certainty and reliable knowledge. Developments in mathematics and the scientific revolution
  • encouraged philosophers to emphasise reason, logical deduction, and clear principles. René
  • Descartes, Baruch Spinoza, and Gottfried Wilhel m Leibniz became the leading representatives of
  • this movement.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the major philosophical aim that shaped Descartes’ intellectual journey. / [CO1] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes’ major philosophical aim was to establish a secure foundation for knowledge by
  • overcoming doubt and uncertainty. He developed the method of systematic doubt to identify
  • truths that could not be questioned, beginning with the cogito. He sought to use these certain
  • foundations to establish further knowledge about the self, God, and the external world.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss Spinoza’s doctrine of intellectual love of God, explaining its origin in adequate and intuitive knowledge. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Spinoza’s doctrine of intellectual love of God (Amor Dei Intellectualis) refers to the highest
  • form of love arising from the rational understanding of God or Nature. It develops through
  • adequate knowledge, which enables the mind to understand things through their true causes and
  • necessary connections. Intuitive knowledge, the highest level of knowledge, allows us to
  • understand particular things as expressions of the infinite nature of God. Through t his
  • understanding, the mind recognises that everything follows necessarily from the nature of God.
  • Intellectual love of God brings lasting joy, freedom from passive emotions, and a deeper
  • understanding of our place in the universe.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Examine the application of the Law of Sufficient Reason to necessary and contingent truths. Explain how Leibniz distinguishes the grounds of these two types of truths. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Leibniz’s law of sufficient reason states that every fact or truth must have a sufficient reason
  • why it is so rather than otherwise. Necessary truths are truths whose opposites involve a
  • contradiction, and they can be established through logical analysis and the principle of
  • contradiction. Contingent truths are truths whose opposites are possible, even though they are
  • actually true. Their sufficient reasons are found in the circumstances, causes, and choices that
  • explain why they occur, ultimately depending on God’s wisdom and choice of the best possible
  • world. Thus, necessary truths rest on logical necessity, whereas contingent truths require
  • sufficient reasons that explain their actual existence without making them logically necessary.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Examine the different grounds employed by Descartes in his initial scepticism and explain how they lead him toward the rejection of uncertain beliefs / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes begins his method of doubt by questioning beliefs that may contain even the
  • slightest uncertainty. First, he uses the argument from sensory illusion, noting that the senses
  • sometimes deceive us. Second, the dream argument suggests that he cannot always distinguish
  • waking experience from dreaming. These arguments lead him to suspend judgment on all beliefs
  • that can be doubted until he discovers an absolutely certain foundation for knowledge.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss Descartes’ theory of substance, explaining the nature and characteristics of infinite substance and finite substances. / [CO2] [12x2 = 24]
questions.solution_html:
• Descartes defines substance as something that exists in such a way that it does not depen d on
  • anything else for its existence, a definition that applies strictly to God alone. Infinite substance
  • refers to God, who is eternal, infinite, omnipotent, and completely independent. Finite substances
  • are created substances that depend on God for their existence. Descartes identifies two principal
  • kinds of finite substance: mind, whose essential attribute is thought, and body, whose essential
  • attribute is extension. Although mind and body are distinct in nature, Descartes maintains that
  • they interact in human beings.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
